rationale: Statement 1 is mostly supported numerically: plane_onrate_baseline matches the recorded value and is close to 1/400000, but the stated absolute deviation (~5e-11) is not exact; it is ~1.25e-11 (relative ~5e-06).
plane_onrate_baseline ≈ 1/n_words is expected null-like behavior for a quality PRNG at this sample size, so it is weak standalone evidence of uniformity.
Statement 2 is supported: boundary_fragility_epsilon=0.0 only establishes no fragility at epsilon=0 in this run, not over an epsilon sweep.
Statement 3 is supported: 51930/399998 = 0.129825649..., consistent with the reported ~0.1298 single-run hit rate.
Statement 4 is supported: 400000/0.0016772940002738324 ≈ 2.3848e8 words/s, correctly interpreted as hardware-specific single-run throughput.
All four statements are explicit and individually falsifiable against the provided record and tolerance rule.
The claim is valid as single-run characterization, not as reproducible or universal performance/structure evidence.
critical_risks: No replicate runs, uncertainty bounds, or seed/hardware variation analysis.
torus_boundary_hits and gen_time_s are point measurements with likely run-to-run variance.
Zero-epsilon fragility result cannot infer behavior at epsilon > 0.
Near-1/n baseline can arise under expected null behavior and does not by itself confirm deeper structure.
Record-level falsification tolerance validates consistency, not cross-run reproducibility.
notes: Adjudication supports the four statements as a scoped single-run report, with a minor arithmetic caveat in Statement 1 wording and major replication limitations. Recommend publication hold until multi-run replication (fixed seed protocol + varied seeds), epsilon sweep for fragility, and variance reporting for boundary hits and timing are added.
